title: Boiled Potato, fresh, peel eaten, with butter

content.title: About
content.content: Boiled potato is a dish made from fresh potatoes cooked in water until tender, with the skin left on and eaten. It is commonly finished with a pat of butter, which adds a smooth, rich flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes are one of the world’s most widely consumed foods, grown in over 125 countries.
Eating the skin boosts fiber, vitamin, and mineral intake.
Butter added to boiled potatoes enhances absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).
Boiled potatoes feature in traditional dishes worldwide, from Russian potato pancakes to Spanish papas a la brava.
When stored properly, boiled potatoes keep in the fridge for up to 5 days.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Boiled potatoes provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Good source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: The skin supplies fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Plain boiled potatoes contain virtually no fat; a modest amount of butter keeps the dish low‑calorie.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Boiled potatoes can raise blood sugar quickly, which may be a concern for people with diabetes.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Although rare, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: Green spots or sprouting indicate solanine, a toxic compound; such parts should be removed.

items.title: Excess butter
items.content: Butter adds saturated fat and calories; use it in moderation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve hot boiled potatoes with a pat of butter on top. They can be eaten plain, added to salads, used in casseroles, or mashed.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep boiled potatoes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 5 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags.
